# @turnprune/opencode

TurnPrune for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 2 (V2 plugin API, 2.0.13 or newer).

Once per user turn, Jev judges the tool outputs of the last turn against your new message. Those no longer needed are replaced by a fixed placeholder, the tool call stays visible, and everything else stays byte-identical. The cached prefix before the first placeholder stays valid, and tool loops stay untouched unless the context window is almost full.

Needs an OpenRouter account with credits. It pays off in long sessions with large tool outputs; in short sessions it can cost more than it saves.

## Install

1. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in the environment (never in a config file). Then open a **new** terminal and restart the background service from there: `opencode service restart`. The service keeps the environment it was started with; restarted from a terminal without the key, it runs without it.
2. `opencode.json`:

   ```json
   { "plugins": ["@turnprune/opencode"] }
   ```

3. `opencode service restart`, then `opencode plugin list` shows `turnprune`. On the first start the package is downloaded; if the list is empty, wait a few seconds and run it again.

## Update

`opencode plugin update @turnprune/opencode`, then `opencode service restart`. `opencode plugin add` does not update an installed plugin; `opencode plugin check` shows whether an update is available.

## Savings

- **Status line** under the prompt: `TurnPrune −12.4k tok (−38%) · Session −41k (−22%)` (current turn, whole session). The package's `./tui` export is loaded by OpenCode's TUI automatically. Without a usable key it says so instead: `TurnPrune: OPENROUTER_API_KEY missing` or `TurnPrune: OpenRouter key rejected`.
- **Command line:** `turnprune stats` (latest session), `--all`, `--session <id>`, `--json`, `--db <path>`. Reads `opencode.db` read-only, needs Node.js ≥ 22.13. Names a missing or rejected key with what to do.

All numbers are TurnPrune's token estimates of the message history (characters ÷ 4, without system prompt and tool definitions), not billed provider tokens. Saved tokens are not saved money: most of the history is cached anyway. For money, use OpenCode's own cost figure.

## Options

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "@turnprune/opencode", "options": { "timeoutMs": 1500, "diagnostic": false } }] }
```

| Option | Environment variable (overrides) | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `TURNPRUNE_ENABLED` | `true` (kill switch) |
| `timeoutMs` | `TURNPRUNE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `1500` (500–5000) |
| `pricingFile` | `TURNPRUNE_PRICING_FILE` | prices from OpenCode's model catalog |
| `diagnostic` | `TURNPRUNE_DIAGNOSTIC` | `false` |

For a local checkout, point the entry at the package directory. OpenCode loads `server.js` (and the TUI part from `tui.js`) from there:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "/abs/path/to/node_modules/@turnprune/opencode" }] }
```

See the [main README](https://github.com/guschi18/turnprune#readme) for how it decides, fail-safe behaviour, limitations, privacy and measured results.
